Third, personality tests are cost-effective and efficient for screening large applicant pools. They can be administered online, scored automatically, and used as a pre-filter before more resource-intensive steps. When combined with other methods (e.g., structured interviews, work samples), they improve the overall predictive validity of the selection system.

Finally, many organizations—from large corporations to public agencies—have successfully used personality assessments for decades. The key is using validated instruments (like the NEO-PI-R or Hogan Assessments) that are job-relevant and legally defensible, rather than off-the-shelf "personal style" quizzes. With proper implementation, personality tests offer valuable insights into how a candidate will actually behave on the job.
